skill.description: Coordinate multiple AI agents with relay messaging, tmux wrappers, and file-based team inbox workflows.

security_audit.summary: No prompt injection text or malicious data-exfiltration intent was found in SKILL.md. All static detections appear to be Markdown examples of relay syntax, CLI commands, or /tmp socket troubleshooting rather than executable code in the skill. The skill still depends on a local relay CLI and should document command approval and secret-handling expectations.

remediation.issue: Markdown command examples may be mistaken for executable behavior.
remediation.suggestion: Add a short safety note that relay commands are examples and should run only after explicit user approval.

remediation.issue: Relay messages can carry sensitive project context if users include it.
remediation.suggestion: Document that users should not send secrets, tokens, credentials, or private customer data through relay messages.

static_findings.snippet: **CRITICAL:** Always end with `>>>` at the end of the last line of content! The `<<<` opens, `>>>` c
**Fallback:** If you forget `>>>`, message auto-closes on double blank line.
Long messages show `[TRUNCATED...]`. Read full content:
Workers run in separate tmux windows and can communicate back via `->relay:` patterns.
| Using bash to send real-time messages | Output `->relay:` directly as text |
| Messages not sending | `relay --status` to check daemon |
| Incomplete message content | `relay read <id>` for full text |
| Pattern not at line start | Move `->relay:` to beginning |
| Forgetting to clear inbox | Use `--clear` flag |

content.value_statement: Multi-agent coding work can lose status, handoffs, and review requests. This skill provides relay patterns, CLI commands, and inbox workflows for coordinated Claude, Codex, and Claude Code agents.
actual_capabilities: Explains tmux relay syntax for direct and broadcast messages.
Lists relay CLI commands for daemon status, shutdown, and agent wrapping.
Shows file-based team inbox commands for asynchronous communication.
Provides patterns for task assignments, status updates, reviews, questions, and blockers.
Describes spawning and releasing worker agents through relay patterns.
Covers bridge usage for communication across multiple projects.
limitations: Requires the relay CLI and daemon to be installed and available.
Does not provide guaranteed delivery or cross-host networking.
Long messages may be truncated and require a follow-up read command.
Does not enforce access controls or secret redaction for message content.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Parallel Coding Agents
use_cases.description: Assign implementation, review, and testing work to separate agents while keeping status visible.

use_cases.title: Run Async Agent Check-ins
use_cases.description: Use the team inbox flow for agents that do not need real-time tmux messaging.

use_cases.title: Bridge Related Projects
use_cases.description: Connect agents working in different project directories and route messages by project and role.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Relay Session
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a small coordinated task.
prompt_templates.prompt: Set up a relay workflow for two agents working on [task]. Name the agents, define their roles, and show the first status message.

prompt_templates.title: Send a Review Handoff
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate handoff between implementer and reviewer.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a relay handoff from [developer agent] to [reviewer agent] for [changed area]. Include context, files to inspect, and expected feedback.

prompt_templates.title: Run Team Inbox Updates
prompt_templates.scenario: Async coordination without real-time tmux windows.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan an async team inbox workflow for [agent names]. Include send, check, clear, and status habits for the task.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Multi-Project Work
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a relay bridge plan for [project list]. Assign lead agents, message routes, escalation rules, and completion signals.

output_examples.input: Coordinate API, frontend, and test agents for an authentication change.
output_examples.output: A relay plan assigns each agent a role, sends initial task messages, defines status broadcasts, and requests review before completion.

output_examples.input: Create an async workflow for agents that check messages periodically.
output_examples.output: The response describes team inbox names, message cadence, clear-after-read behavior, and a final summary routine.

output_examples.input: Plan cross-project messaging for backend and web client repositories.
output_examples.output: The response maps each project to a relay route, assigns leads, and defines when agents should broadcast blockers or completion.

best_practices: Use fenced relay messages for multi-line updates and review requests.
Read full truncated messages before responding to avoid missing context.
Keep secrets, tokens, and credentials out of relay messages.
anti_patterns: Using relay coordination for a single-agent task.
Assuming relay provides guaranteed message delivery.
Sending sensitive credentials or private data through agent messages.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps multiple AI agents coordinate work through relay messages, team inbox commands, and tmux-based workflows.

faq.question: Does it require the relay CLI?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented workflows assume the relay command and daemon are available in the local environment.

faq.question: Can it work without tmux?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill also describes file-based team inbox commands for asynchronous coordination.

faq.question: Is message delivery guaranteed?
faq.answer: No. The skill states it should not be used when guaranteed delivery is required.

faq.question: Can it coordinate Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill describes real-time collaboration patterns for Claude, Codex, Gemini, and Claude Code style agents.

faq.question: Should secrets be sent through relay messages?
faq.answer: No. Keep credentials, tokens, and sensitive customer data out of relay messages.
